name: Trading processes
description: How an order becomes a settled trade, from the customer pressing buy to the balance moving. Does not cover onboarding, funding or reporting — those are separate packs.

processes.name: Trade
processes.description: A customer converts one asset into another at a price the platform is willing to honour, and both sides of the exchange are recorded so the books balance.

processes.name: Place an order
processes.description: Everything between the customer submitting an order and that order being accepted for matching: validating it, pricing it, and durably recording it.

processes.name: Validate and price the order
processes.description: Checks the customer may trade, that they hold enough of the asset they are selling, and attaches the rate the order will be matched against. A rejection here never reaches the matching engine.
processes.trigger: The customer submits an order through the app or the public API.
processes.outcome: The order is priced and persisted as PENDING, or rejected with a reason the customer can act on.

steps.name: Receive the order
steps.description: The gateway terminates the customer session and forwards the order; from here on the customer id is trusted.

steps.name: Check the customer may trade
steps.description: Reads the KYC state. A customer who has not passed verification is rejected here rather than later, so the rejection is fast and explainable.

steps.name: Check the balance covers the order
steps.description: Reads the live wallet balance. This is a check, not a reservation — the funds are only moved once the order matches, so an order can still fail later if the balance moves underneath it.

steps.name: Attach the rate
steps.description: Takes the quote from the local Redis copy when it is fresh, and calls pricing only on a miss. The cache is what keeps order placement fast during a market move.

steps.name: Call pricing on a cache miss
steps.description: Only runs when the cached quote is missing or stale.

steps.name: Persist the order
steps.description: Writes the order as PENDING before anything is published, so a crash between here and the publish leaves a recoverable record rather than a lost order.

processes.name: Route the order to matching
processes.description: Publishes the accepted order for the matching engine to pick up. The publish is the handover point: once it succeeds, order-service is no longer responsible for the outcome.
processes.trigger: An order has been persisted as PENDING by 2.1.1.
processes.outcome: The order is on the wire and the matching engine owns it.

steps.name: Publish the order
steps.description: Keyed by instrument so one instrument's orders stay in sequence on a single partition.

steps.name: Pick the order up
steps.description: The matching engine holds its book in memory; this consume is how an order enters it.

processes.name: Match and settle
processes.description: Turning a resting order into an executed trade, and moving the money so the books and the customer's balance agree.

processes.name: Match the order
processes.description: Crosses the order against the book. Unmatched orders rest until they match, expire or are cancelled — this process only covers the matching itself.
processes.trigger: An order arrives on orders.placed.v1, or a price tick moves the book.
processes.outcome: A fill is published, or the order rests.

steps.name: Keep the book priced
steps.description: Market ticks continuously reprice the resting book; a tick can trigger a match with no new order involved.

steps.name: Publish the fill
steps.description: One event per fill. A large order that fills in parts produces several, all carrying the same order id.

processes.name: Post the trade to the ledger
processes.description: Writes the double-entry postings for the fill. This is the point the trade becomes real for accounting, and it must be idempotent because the fill event can be redelivered.
processes.trigger: A fill is published on orders.matched.v1.
processes.outcome: Balanced postings exist for both legs of the trade.

steps.name: Write the postings
steps.description: Both legs in one transaction, keyed on the fill id so a redelivered event is a no-op rather than a double posting.

processes.name: Move the customer balance
processes.description: Updates the wallet the customer actually sees, and announces the change for anything downstream that cares.
processes.trigger: A fill is published on orders.matched.v1.
processes.outcome: The customer's visible balance reflects the trade.

steps.name: Apply the fill to the wallet
Announce the new balance
steps.description: Consumed by notification and reporting. Carries the balance after the change, not the delta.

processes.name: Tell the customer
processes.description: Getting the fill in front of the customer, through whichever channel they have enabled.

processes.name: Send the fill notification
processes.description: Fans the balance change out to email and push. Best-effort: a failure here never blocks the trade, which has already settled by this point.
processes.trigger: A balance change is announced on wallet.balance.changed.v1.
processes.outcome: The customer has been told, or the failure has been logged and dropped.

steps.name: Send the message
steps.description: Channel and locale come from the customer's notification preferences.
